analysis.investment_thesis: Affle 3i is a genuine quality compounder — 45% revenue CAGR over 7 years, consistently positive FCF, net cash balance sheet, and a differentiated CPCU mobile advertising model with emerging market tailwinds. The problem is simple: at 47x P/E with a FCF yield of just 1.3% and EV/EBITDA of 40x, every possible good outcome is already priced in and there is no margin of safety whatsoever.
key_strengths: Exceptional compounding: revenue grew from INR 167 Cr (FY18) to INR 2,266 Cr (FY25) at 45% CAGR while maintaining FCF positivity every year — real business, not accounting fiction
Fortress balance sheet: net cash of ~INR 965 Cr, debt-free in practice (total debt INR 82 Cr vs cash INR 1,047 Cr), no permanent capital loss risk from leverage
CPCU business model — paying only for converted users — creates natural advertiser loyalty and differentiates Affle from pure impression-based competitors
key_risks: FCF yield of 1.3% (INR 266 Cr FCF on INR 20,649 Cr market cap) — to earn a 12% annual return from here, FCF must reach INR 830 Cr within 5 years, requiring 25%+ sustained annual FCF growth
Mobile advertising is dominated globally by Google and Meta; any acceleration of their programmatic push into Indian emerging markets could compress Affle's CPCU pricing

Five acquisitions (Appnext, Mediasmart, Jampp, RevX, YouAppi) create integration complexity and latent goodwill impairment risk — total assets grew from INR 402 Cr (FY20) to INR 3,914 Cr (FY25), much of it intangible
red_flags: EV/EBITDA of 40x with no net debt — for an adtech company in a competitive global market, this prices in 7+ years of flawless execution with zero competitive response
Other income of INR 94 Cr in FY25 equals 24% of operating income — quality of reported earnings deserves scrutiny
Consensus is uniformly bullish on the India digital advertising story — when everyone agrees, the market has already moved; there are no cheap seats left
analysis.detailed_analysis: Affle is the highest-quality business in this group on operational metrics. The CPCU model generates genuine advertiser stickiness, and growing from INR 167 Cr to INR 2,266 Cr in revenue while maintaining positive FCF throughout is an enviable record. Management has executed a deliberate global expansion acquiring programmatic platforms across geographies. Net cash on the balance sheet means no leverage-driven downside — the only way to permanently lose capital here is through competitive disruption or valuation mean-reversion.
